pr_title: Add dependency injection support for object pools
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48172

_In draft until the API review is done_
pr_comments: What happened to the open generic idea?

@davidfowl I am trying to implement the open generic version but I am facing an issue. We need an interface like `IObjectPool<>` to resolve and object pool for a specific type but we can't use a definition type as the generic argument, only the implementation type. So instead of being able to write `provider.GetService<IObjectPool<ITestClass>>()` you need to write `provider.GetService<IObjectPool<TestClass>>()` which is breaking the expected usage.

If you believe in something it helps a lot.
I made a branch with the open generic version, let me know if you prefer this one and I'll replace the PR (and api issue).

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/compare/main...sebros/opengenerics

Check the `Pooled<T>` usage in the tests that could also be exposed directly as extension methods on `IServiceCollection` -> `AddScopedPooled<ITestClass, TestClass>()` for instance.
Pool options needs to be per type and global right?
This PR should be closed at this point, right? Given https://github.com/dotnet/extensions/pull/4038.

Looks like this PR hasn't been active for some time and the codebase could have been changed in the meantime.
To make sure no breaking changes are introduced, please leave an `/azp run` comment here to rerun the CI pipeline and confirm success before merging the change.

issue_context.title: Dependency Injected pooled instances
comments: This looks like minimal DI support for adding a closed generic object pool. That seems fine. I would also remove the ConfigurePools overload that takes `IConfigurationSection`.

> adding a closed generic object pool

Do you think an open generic would make more sense? Are there inherent challenges?

I feel like the open generic makes more sense for this. 

```C#
services.AddObjectPools()
```

Thank you for submitting this for API review. This will be reviewed by @dotnet/aspnet-api-review at the next meeting of the ASP.NET Core API Review group. Updated with open generic design. Branch is here: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/compare/main...sebros/opengenerics

API Review Notes:

- What dll is this going into?
  - It will depend on both Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions and Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool.
  - Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool has no dependency on M.E.DI. And there's no dependency in the other direction either.
  - The namespace is proposed as Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Pools.
  - Can we add a M.E.DI dependency to Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool?
- Is this a new DI lifetime? Is "pooled" similar to singleton/scoped/transient?
  - We're considering core DI changes for named services.
- "Pooling objects with scoped/transient dependencies might leak services across requests that are not meant to be reused" seems like a serious risk.
  - Does making the pooled objects resettable mitigate this?
    - That wouldn't help if you pooled a DbContext which is then disposed.
  - In practice, the pooled resources can only depend on singletons and transient services.
- This could be useful for M.E.ML
- The open generic proposal is preferred by @sebastienros even though it's an "alternative"
  - The open generic proposal seems to make the risk of misusing the pool for scoped service worse. Now a caller can resolve any service from a pool.
  - Or you could say this is more like `IOptions<TOptions>` which people don't really seem to misuse.
    - But `IOptions<TOptions>` uses `new()` not `ActivatorUtilities`.
  - Let's leave it up to library authors and service registering code to say what is pooled.
- How are the types activated?
  - ActivatorUtilities. They can resolve services.
- Does `where TDefinition : IResettable` mitigate misusage?
  - Requiring `IResettable` is annoying. What if you just want to pool `StringBuilder` or something else that doesn't implement `IResettable`? Being forced to wrap it would be annoying. 
- How do you use a custom `PooledObjectPolicy`?
  - You cannot, because DI is defining its own `PooledObjectPolicy`.
  - Why can't we add an overload that takes `IPooledObjectPolicy<TImplementation>`? Could be useful for using `StringBuilderPooledObjectPolicy`.
  - We could also consider trying to resolve `IPooledObjectPolicy<TImplementation>` as a service and using that if it exists. That would allow custom policies to user services.
- `AddPool` -> `AddPooled`? Pro and con, sounds a lot like a new lifetime and it's not (e.g. `AddScoped`, `AddSingleton`, `AddTransient`).
  - We like it.
- What about `DependencyInjectionExtensions`?
  - Maybe `ObjectPoolServiceCollectionExtensions`.
- What does `ConfigurePools` do?
  - We didn't get to this.

Here's what we're thinking so far.

```csharp
// Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool.dll
namespace Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool;

public static class ObjectPoolServiceCollectionExtensions
{
    public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TDefinition>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions>? configure = null) 
        where TDefinition : class

    public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TDefinition, TImplementation>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions>? configure = null)
        where TDefinition : class
        where TImplementation : class, TDefinition

    public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TDefinition, TImplementation>(this IServiceCollection services, IPooledObjectPolicy<TImplementation> pooledObjectPolicy, Action<PoolOptions>? configure = null)
        where TDefinition : class
        where TImplementation : class, TDefinition

    public static IServiceCollection ConfigurePools(this IServiceCollection services, IConfigurationSection section)
}

public sealed class PoolOptions
{
    public int Capacity { get; set; } = Environment.ProcessorCount * 2;
}
```

Note: M.E.DI = Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions

New dll and add it to the shared framework. I'm not sure about the ConfigurePools (also why not IConfiguration vs IConfigurationSection). I think we need the ability to configure per pool type and for all pools so its possible pool options will need to be generic?

Updated proposal:
- Rename `configure` to `configureOptions` to match the standard `Configure` extension method.
- Add generic version of `ConfigurePools()` to target a specific pool

```diff
// Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool.dll
namespace Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool;

public static class ObjectPoolServiceCollectionExtensions
{
    public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TDefinition>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions>? configure = null) 
        where TDefinition : class

-   public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TDefinition, TImplementation>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions>? configure = null)
+   public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TDefinition, TImplementation>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions>? configureOptions = null)
        where TDefinition : class
        where TImplementation : class, TDefinition

-   public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TDefinition, TImplementation>(this IServiceCollection services, IPooledObjectPolicy<TImplementation> pooledObjectPolicy, Action<PoolOptions>? configure = null)
+   public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TDefinition, TImplementation>(this IServiceCollection services, IPooledObjectPolicy<TImplementation> pooledObjectPolicy, Action<PoolOptions>? configureOptions = null)
        where TDefinition : class
        where TImplementation : class, TDefinition

-   public static IServiceCollection ConfigurePools(this IServiceCollection services, IConfigurationSection section)
+   public static IServiceCollection ConfigurePools(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions> configureOptions)
    
+   public static IServiceCollection ConfigurePools<TDefinition>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions> configureOptions)
+       where TDefinition : class    
}

public sealed class PoolOptions
{
    public int Capacity { get; set; } = Environment.ProcessorCount * 2;
}
```

API Review Notes:

- Should `TDefinition` be called `TService` to match DI?
  - It's not exactly a service, but it sounds better than `TDefinition` which sounds too similar to `TImplementation`.
  - `TPooled`? It's not obvious what it means.
- What happens if `builder.Services.Configure<PoolOptions>(() => ...)`? Do these configure methods get called before the specific `AddPooled`?
- Could we have a `ConfigurePools(IConfiguration)` that configures each pool independently keyed by fully qualified type name?
  - Can this use named options?
    - The per-type configuration already is.
  - Is there a similar API we've shipped that has cascading global, and per-type options? AuthenticationOptions don't work that way.
- Does it make sense to change a global default at all? Isn't it very specific to what is being pooled?
  - Maybe we can avoid doing this. It's something that could potentially added later if necessary.
  - For now at least.`builder.Services.Configure<PoolOptions>(() => ...)` does nothing.
- Is the `ConfigurePools<TDefinition>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions> configureOptions)` necessary? You can configure during the call to `AddPooled`.
  - Could be useful if an extension method added a pool internally you want to reconfigure.
  - Manually using named options is annoying.
  - Figuring out the right key could require looking at the docs or implementation.
  - We can also add the extra config methods later.
  - If you want to use the same internal `TImplementation` that a library added in an extension method but reconfigure the count using just the `TService`, it could be useful.
- Do we need an `AddPooled` overload that accepts a `IPooledObjectPolicy<TImplementation>`?
  - If you really want to do this, you can add the `ObjectPool<TImplementation>` to DI yourself.
- Should `ConfigurePools<TService>` be called `ConfigurePool<TService>` or `ConfigurePooled<TService>`?
  - Let's make it singular `ConfigurPool` instead
- Does `AddPooled` override previous calls with the same `TService` but a different `TImplementation`?
  - Yes. If it didn't, we should call it `TryAddPooled`.
- Would we consider `AddPool` or `AddObjectPool` over `AddPooled`?
  - Everyone like `AddPooled`.

API Approved!

```diff
// Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool.dll
namespace Microsoft.Extensions.ObjectPool;

+ public static class ObjectPoolServiceCollectionExtensions
+ {
+    public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TService>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions>? configure = null) 
+        where TService : class
+
+   public static IServiceCollection AddPooled<TService, TImplementation>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions>? configureOptions = null)
+        where TService : class
+        where TImplementation : class, TService
+
+   public static IServiceCollection ConfigurePool<TService>(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PoolOptions> configureOptions)
+       where TService : class    
+ }

+ public sealed class PoolOptions
+ {
+    public int Capacity { get; set; } = Environment.ProcessorCount * 2;
+ }
```
I'm assuming we can now close this one as no longer planned given that we've added [a library that does it in dotnet/extensions repo](https://github.com/dotnet/extensions/pull/4038)?
Closing this for now due to the above. Feel free to reopen if needed.

review_comments: The idea is that `Configure<PoolOptions>(typeof(TService).FullName)` should still be called to register an instance of the options with the default value for this type. So if no specific lambda is passed, it will call it with and empty one.
I still don't get it. What breaks if you use the suggested code above?

3 lines after that it uses `GetRequiredService`. If this is not called with an empty lambda then the `GetRequiredService` will fail. I will change this code to use `GetService` instead and return a new `PoolOptions` if it is not resolved since it seems confusing.
I put this in a test but this could also be an extension method directly usable. The usage pattern is nice IMO.
